The equation of the line ${l}_{1}$ is $y=-4x-3$ and ${l}_{2}$ is perpendicular to ${l}_{1}.$  What is the equation of ${l}_{2}?$

$y=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
Since perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other, the slope of ${l}_{2}$ is the negative reciprocal of the slope of ${l}_{1}.$ Since ${l}_{1}$ has a slope of $-4,$ the line ${l}_{2}$ must have a slope of $\frac{1}{4}.$

Our perpendicular line must have the slope $m=\frac{1}{4}$ and pass through the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(4,2).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-2 & =\frac{1}{4}(x-4) \\ y-2 & =\frac{1}{4}x-1 \\ y & =\frac{1}{4}x+1\end{aligned}
$$
